subject: psychiatry
title: Parasomnias, Obstructive Sleep Apnoea, and Sleep Therapeutics

steps.tx: **Modafinil** serves as the first-line wakefulness-promoting pharmacological agent for excessive daytime sleepiness in narcolepsy, obstructive sleep apnoea, and shift work sleep disorder. Acting primarily as a selective dopamine reuptake inhibitor while indirectly activating hypothalamic orexin and histamine systems, modafinil carries significantly lower abuse liability than traditional stimulants.
steps.say: Modafinil promotes daytime alertness in narcolepsy by selectively blocking dopamine reuptake and activating hypothalamic orexin, with low abuse risk.

left.title: Modafinil Profile
points: Selective dopamine transporter (DAT) block
Activates tuberomammillary histamine neurons
Promotes clean wakefulness without euphoria
Minimal cardiovascular sympathomimetic strain

right.title: Traditional Stimulants
points: Dextroamphetamine & methylphenidate
Massive monoamine release and reuptake block
High risk of euphoria, tolerance, and addiction
Severe tachycardia and arterial hypertension

steps.tx: **Obstructive sleep apnoea**, abbreviated OSA, is characterized by repetitive complete cessation (apnoea) or partial reduction (hypopnoea) of upper pharyngeal airflow during sleep, caused by muscular pharyngeal collapse despite persistent respiratory effort. It produces daytime sleepiness, morning headaches, loud snoring, and secondary polycythaemia.
steps.say: Obstructive sleep apnoea features repetitive pharyngeal collapse with loud snoring and daytime sleepiness, diagnosed when the AHI exceeds five per hour.

vis.title: Apnoea-Hypopnoea Index (AHI) Strata
rows: Positional therapy, weight loss, mandibular splints
Mandatory nocturnal CPAP; evaluate bariatric surgery

steps.tx: **Continuous positive airway pressure**, abbreviated CPAP, serves as the definitive non-surgical gold standard treatment for moderate to severe obstructive sleep apnoea. A bedside pneumatic pump delivers pressurized ambient air through a nasal or facial mask, pneumatically splinting the collapsible pharyngeal airway open throughout inspiration and expiration.
steps.say: Continuous positive airway pressure splints the pharynx open with pressurized air, eliminating apnoeas, oxygen desaturations, and daytime sleepiness.

nodes.label: Nocturnal loss of pharyngeal dilator muscle tone triggers airway collapse
CPAP machine delivers constant positive pneumatic air pressure
Pharyngeal airway splinted open, preventing apnoea and desaturation
Restoration of continuous deep sleep and reduction of cardiac risk

steps.tx: **Somnambulism**, or sleepwalking, is an arousal parasomnia arising from slow-wave NREM stage N3 sleep, most commonly encountered in children between four and eight years of age. Individuals initiate complex motor behaviors, such as walking or dressing, while displaying blank staring eyes and total amnesia for the episode.
steps.say: Somnambulism is an NREM stage N3 parasomnia where patients walk with open, unseeing eyes during deep sleep, with total amnesia upon waking.

vis.title: NREM Parasomnia Spectrum
rows: NREM Stage N3 (First third of night)
Complex motor ambulation; unarousable; secure doors & windows
NREM Stage N3 (First third of night)
Piercing scream; intense autonomic panic; zero dream recall
NREM Stage N3 (First third of night)
Disorientation in bed; slurred speech; no ambulation or terror

steps.tx: **Night terrors versus nightmares** represents a critical clinical differential in pediatric and adult sleep psychiatry. Night terrors arise from deep NREM stage N3 sleep during the first third of the night, featuring autonomic terror and amnesia; nightmares arise from REM sleep during the final third, with vivid dream recall.
steps.say: Night terrors occur in early N3 sleep with autonomic panic and amnesia. Nightmares occur in late REM sleep with vivid dream recall and alertness.

left.title: Night Terrors (NREM Stage N3)
points: Occurs during the first third of the night
Piercing vocal scream and autonomic panic
Patient is glassy-eyed and unarousable
Total amnesia for the event in the morning

right.title: Nightmares (REM Sleep)
points: Occurs during the final third of the night
Wakes up immediately alert and oriented
Vivid, detailed narrative dream recall
Autonomic arousal is mild to moderate

steps.tx: **REM sleep behaviour disorder**, abbreviated RBD, is characterized by the loss of normal electromyographic muscle atonia during REM sleep, resulting in vigorous, violent dream-enacting behaviors. Patients punch, kick, or leap from bed while dreaming of being attacked, frequently injuring themselves or bed partners.
steps.say: REM sleep behaviour disorder involves loss of normal dream atonia, causing violent dream enactment. It strongly predicts future Parkinson disease.

vis.title: RBD Neurodegenerative Link
rows: Loss of REM muscle atonia on chin/tibialis EMG
Polysomnography confirms motor activity during REM
Strong prodromal marker for Parkinson disease or DLB
Precedes motor parkinsonism by 10 to 15 years
Provides crucial window for neuroprotective trials
Clonazepam (0.5 to 1.0 mg) or high-dose melatonin
Suppresses dream enactment and restores safety

steps.tx: **Restless legs syndrome**, also known as Willis-Ekbom disease, is a sensorimotor disorder characterized by an irresistible urge to move the legs, accompanied by uncomfortable creeping sensations. Symptoms occur predominantly at rest, worsen in the evening, and achieve immediate, temporary relief with physical movement.
steps.say: Restless legs syndrome involves an irresistible urge to move the legs at rest with evening worsening, linked to brain iron deficiency and dopamine dysfunction.

nodes.label: U: Urge to move legs, usually with uncomfortable sensations
R: Rest triggers or worsens symptoms (sitting or lying down)
G: Gets better with movement (walking, stretching, rubbing)
E: Evening or night worsening of symptoms

steps.tx: **Circadian rhythm sleep-wake disorders** involve a chronic misalignment between an individual's endogenous circadian sleep-wake pacemaker and external societal schedules. Delayed sleep phase syndrome features sleep onset delayed until 3 to 6 AM with waking at noon; advanced sleep phase syndrome features evening sleepiness by 7 PM.
steps.say: Circadian disorders misalign internal sleep timing with society, such as delayed sleep phase where sleep is delayed until early morning hours.

left.title: Delayed Sleep Phase Syndrome
points: Common in adolescents and young adults
Sleep onset typically between 2 AM and 6 AM
Severe difficulty waking for school or morning work
Treated with evening melatonin & morning bright light

right.title: Advanced Sleep Phase Syndrome
points: Common in elderly populations
Sleep onset between 6 PM and 9 PM
Awakening early morning between 2 AM and 5 AM
Treated with evening bright light therapy
